subject: words
title: Short for two words
about: Contractions: two words squeezed into one, with an apostrophe standing in for the missing letters (can't is short for cannot). CKLA Grade 1 teaches contractions in Unit 4 grammar and his readers are full of them; NC's L.1.2 conventions list puts apostrophes in grades 2 and 3, so reading them is the goal here, not spelling them.
tip: Say the two long words, then squeeze them together fast and ask which letters fell out where the apostrophe is.

cards.note: can't is short for cannot. The apostrophe stands for the missing n and o.
don't is short for do not. The apostrophe stands for the missing o. The o in don't says its name.
isn't is short for is not. The apostrophe stands for the missing o.
didn't is short for did not. The apostrophe stands for the missing o.
wasn't is short for was not. The apostrophe stands for the missing o.
aren't is short for are not. The apostrophe stands for the missing o.
won't is short for will not. This one changes its spelling: will turns into wo.
it's is short for it is. The apostrophe stands for the missing i.
he's is short for he is. The apostrophe stands for the missing i.
she's is short for she is. The apostrophe stands for the missing i.
that's is short for that is. The apostrophe stands for the missing i.
let's is short for let us. The apostrophe stands for the missing u.
I'm is short for I am. The apostrophe stands for the missing a. I is always a capital.
I've is short for I have. The apostrophe stands for the missing h and a.
I'll is short for I will. The apostrophe stands for the missing w and i.
we'll is short for we will. The apostrophe stands for the missing w and i.
you'll is short for you will. The apostrophe stands for the missing w and i.
you're is short for you are. The apostrophe stands for the missing a.
we're is short for we are. The apostrophe stands for the missing a.
they're is short for they are. The apostrophe stands for the missing a.
